requirement_text.REQ-002:
Depends on REQ-001a and REQ-001b (both merged), which together establish messages/ru.json and messages/uz.json with 177 keys across 13 namespaces (Metadata + 12 landing-component namespaces), currently with every uz value a placeholder duplicate of the ru value. This requirement replaces every placeholder in messages/uz.json with an actual Uzbek (O'zbek, Latin script -- the modern standard orthography, not Cyrillic Uzbek) translation, following docs/guides/content_ba_guide.md's voice/casing/vocabulary rules (functional operator-facing tone, no exclamation marks or slogans, sentence case for buttons/menu items, Title Case for section/page titles mapping to a domain noun, UPPERCASE MONO for status labels) applied to Uzbek rather than Russian prose.

Domain vocabulary decision (already made, apply as stated, do not re-decide): the design system's domain vocabulary terms -- Event, Chapter, Talk, Speaker, CFP, Agenda, Check-in, Going, Watching -- STAY IN ENGLISH VERBATIM in the Uzbek copy, exactly as they already do in the Russian copy per content_ba_guide.md SS4 ('use verbatim, don't invent synonyms'). Surrounding sentence structure, headings, and connecting prose around these terms are still fully translated into Uzbek -- only the specific vocabulary tokens listed remain untranslated. None of the current 177 keys' values actually contain these exact domain-vocabulary terms as standalone values (verify this yourself by scanning messages/ru.json -- if you find a key whose value IS one of these terms verbatim, leave it unchanged in uz; if a term appears embedded inside a longer sentence, translate the surrounding sentence and keep the term itself in English).

Scope: every one of the 177 keys in messages/uz.json (3 Metadata keys + 174 keys across the 12 landing-component namespaces: Band, Creed, Doors, Events, Footer, Hero, MapSection, Metrics, Nav, Partners, Streams, Team).

task.description: You are on branch feature/WF02-REQ-002 -- verify with git branch --show-current before editing anything. Read messages/ru.json in full to get the real, current Russian source strings for every one of the 177 keys (do not use any paraphrased version from this handoff -- the file is the source of truth). Read messages/uz.json to confirm its current placeholder state (every value currently byte-identical to ru.json's, except ogLocale which is already 'uz_UZ'). Write real Uzbek (Latin-script) translations for every one of the 174 non-domain-vocabulary-affected keys, replacing the ru-duplicated placeholder in messages/uz.json in place -- same JSON structure, same key names, only the values change. Follow content_ba_guide.md's voice rules applied to Uzbek: functional/operator-facing tone (no exclamation marks, slogans, or AI-generated-sounding clichés), sentence case for buttons/menu items, Title Case for section/page headings mapping to a domain noun, UPPERCASE MONO preserved for any status-label-shaped values (check MapSection/Streams status values specifically -- their Russian source uses lowercase status words like 'активен'/'в планах' which the guide's casing rule may or may not apply to at the value level -- read the actual rendered component context if genuinely ambiguous, and state your reasoning rather than guessing silently). Preserve the two t.rich()-consumed keys (Hero.title, Creed.quote) exactly in their current structure -- they contain literal `...` markup in the Russian source (check this yourself) that next-intl's t.rich() parses at render time; your Uzbek translation must keep the SAME `` tag placement semantics (wrapping the equivalent emphasized clause in the Uzbek sentence), not necessarily the same character positions. Do not touch messages/ru.json. Do not touch any file under src/ or public/.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of the 177 keys in messages/uz.json has a real Uzbek Latin-script value (not a byte-for-byte Russian duplicate), except any key whose value is verified to be a standalone domain-vocabulary term per content_ba_guide.md SS4 -- state explicitly in your result if any such key was found and left verbatim, or state that none were found
No Cyrillic characters remain anywhere in messages/uz.json's values (verified by a Unicode Cyrillic-range regex scan you run yourself)
The two t.rich()-consumed keys (Hero.title, Creed.quote) retain valid, correctly-placed ... markup around the Uzbek equivalent of the originally emphasized clause
No exclamation marks, slogans, or emoji introduced anywhere in messages/uz.json
messages/ru.json is completely untouched (verify with git diff after your edits)
npm run build still passes after your edit (JSON validity + no next-intl runtime issues)
